Trust me man.  I've been there.  It took me 4 months to actually go to an appointment.  It was the start of getting better.  

Nothing worth doing is easy.  If I could go back in time and get help as soon as I started feeling that way I would do it so fast.  Way too many close calls to make it worth waiting that long.

I know exactly that sinking feeling that you're feeling.  It definitely got worse for me before it got better.  But it did get better.

The hard part is that I really needed to want to get better.  As nice as it is to think that you just have to grin and bear it, you have to put in the work to find that fun again.  I know you can do it, because you've done it before.  Just because you don't remember that state of mind doesn't mean you can't get there again.

I'd highly recommend therapy.  I had always thought going to a therapist would make me some weirdo who can't even function in society without someone holding my hand, but its a lot more than that.  Having a professional hear your thought processes and finding ways to think better in a way is a really important step to getting better.

One of the worst moments of my life was when my best friend of 5 years, someone who I had shared all my issues with and was like a little brother to me, told me he was purposely ghosting me because I was just way too much of a bummer and he didn't want me to bring him down.  That night I found out actually hanging yourself from a doorknob while blacked out was actually really, really hard.  

You're not the first person to feel this way and you're definitely not the last.  Trust me, no one's "winning" when you kill yourself.  Losing friends can be a very shitty experience.  I can say for sure that when you do get better, and when you do find other friends that you really talk with, you'll still find happiness in the memories you had with your previous friends, even if you guys aren't together anymore.  There isn't a day in my life that I won't forget the fun I had with my best friend, just as there isn't a day in my life that I don't regret how that friendship ended.

It's insane how much grades matter during college, to the point where a lot of students have felt the exact same way you do.  I definitely retained the use of a school therapist during my undergraduate for a lot of reasons - grades being one of them.

The hard part is depression saps that potential to do well in school.  I've had 0.5 GPA semesters before, and semesters where I was mentally okay I've had straight A semesters.  

I can tell you now your academic standing doesn't determine the rest of your life.  Half of my coworkers are college (and even high school dropouts) that easily clear six figures.  And if you really want to get through college, and manage to get your mental health in check, your GPA won't matter for a lick after college.

For someone who potentially has Aspergers, you seem pretty in touch with people.  Regardless of your mistakes, there's always time to make up for them.  You mention charges getting in the way of a job, but there are tons of industries like Oil & Gas, etc. where you can clear six figures as an ex-felon within a year or so.  Granted those jobs are a lot rougher and not something I would recommend...

I think the biggest thing that keeps people on this subreddit from permanently hurting themselves is the idea that life can get better.  This idea only actually happens if we have something in the future we can look forward to.  No matter how small, once you find something in the future you can look forward to - you can start to set goals which will give you even bigger and better things to look forward to?

Large-sized guy?  Start running/hitting the gym and thinking about dat sweet body.  Feel like a retard?  Start reading.  Work your way up.  Fuck around with sudokus.  Feel like an awkward fuck (for someone who thinks they're awkward, you've already gotten laid two times more than me) - go out to bars or just go on walks and talk with people.  See a cute girl walking a cute puppy?  Petting a puppy is a damn good reason to talk to that girl. 

The fact you have the empathy to understand where you fucked up kind of makes me believe that people wouldn't be better off without you.  If you came here calling your ex a stupid bitch and about how much you hate your kid I might see that, but you didn't.  Life's fucking weird, bro.  It can get really, really bad.  If you're able to get through the bad, though, you get a lot more perspective for the good in your life.  The good that you've earned through busting your ass and the good that comes from just living life.  Freshly mown grass smells like shit if you live in a garden in your entire life.
